raw_response:
I'm 64 years old, farming these 10.1 mu in Quzhou County for 38 years now. It's just me and the wife — our kids went to the city long ago. We're not young anymore, so every decision has to account for what our backs can still handle and what we have to pay others to do.

I keep about 6.5 mu in wheat-maize double cropping and 3.6 mu in cotton. The wheat went in last October — I plowed the fields in September and put down base fertilizer at planting, about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. Now it's early April and the wheat is greening up. The extension fellow was around saying to topdress 15 kg urea per mu at jointing, but I've done this long enough to trust my own eyes. I'll put down about 20 jin of urea per mu at jointing — that's around 10 kg — because that's what gave me a decent yield the last few years. I'll irrigate three times: once now as it greens up, once at jointing, and a third time at heading if the spring stays dry. Pumping water costs money, but you can't cheat wheat on water, not if you want to pay the bills.

The cotton needs to go in by late April on that 3.6 mu. I buy hybrid seed from the county supply shop — about 35 yuan per mu. I'll plow and bed those fields, put down base fertilizer before planting, then topdress once when it starts flowering. Two irrigations should do, maybe three if July turns scorching. The real headache with cotton is the picking. Me and the wife can manage the planting and spraying, but picking 3.6 mu at our age? No, I'll hire the village women for that. It's extra cost but there's no choice. I'll also spray for bollworm and weeds — cotton always needs more pesticide than grain.

Then comes maize in mid-June, right after wheat harvest. That turnaround is always brutal — sometimes only five or six days between cutting wheat and getting maize in the ground. I hire the combine for wheat, then plant maize either with the hand planter or get Old Wang's tractor if he's free. Hybrid maize seed is about 45 yuan per mu. I put fertilizer in the planting hole — some compound and urea, about 15 kg nitrogen per mu total. Maybe one more topdress if the plants look pale. Summer rains usually help, but last July was dry and I got burned, so I'll plan to irrigate twice to be safe.

Money is tight. Seed, fertilizer, pesticide, water pumping, and hired labor — I'm looking at around 3,200 yuan this year. That's a big chunk for two old people. But if wheat gives me 450 kg per mu, maize about 480 kg per mu, and cotton 230 kg per mu, we'll get by. I'm keeping some cash back though. At our age, doctor bills can come any time. Better to have a little saved than to regret it.
